Meeting 25/2569 · Subcommittee on Older Persons, Persons with Disabilities and the Disadvantaged
Preparing the 12 November seminar, and a draft report on education for persons with disabilities
se: The meeting prepared the seminar on population structure and quality of life on Thursday 12 November 2026 at the Parliament House; for the topic of technology and innovation for older persons, it agreed to invite the National Science and Technology Development Agency and an association of health and elderly care businesses. It then considered the draft report on education for persons with disabilities, which notes that 2,326,639 people held disability cards as of 31 August 2026, and that education for persons with disabilities is a basic right, not welfare. It also considered 2 more draft reports: other countries' policies to encourage childbirth, and an evaluation of the law on employment of older persons in the private sector, with King Prajadhipok's Institute.
it: Preparing the seminar on population structure and quality of life, 12 November 2026
Draft study report on education for persons with disabilities
Draft report on other countries' policies to encourage childbirth, to address the ageing society
Draft report evaluating the law on employment of older persons in the private sector

Oversight of elderly care homes and protecting older people from violence
se: The meeting considered the oversight of elderly care homes and ways to protect older people from violence, with the Department of Health Service Support and the Department of Local Administration. On the local side, about 14 million people are registered for the old-age allowance, and an Interior Ministry rule sets up local care volunteers who visit homebound and bedbound older people. The Department of Health Service Support said carers must complete 420 hours of training and one carer may look after no more than 5 beds; about 340,000 older people are homebound or bedbound, while care homes have about 26,000 beds. Proposals received included a national strategic plan to bring budgets and direction down to provinces and local areas.
it: Oversight of elderly care homes and ways to protect older people from violence
The local role: the old-age allowance, local health security funds and local care volunteers
Carer standards (420 hours of training, no more than 5 beds per carer) and the shortage of beds
Proposals to amend the law so foreign workers can be assistant carers under Thai carers, and for a national strategic plan

Helping people live long, healthy lives with science and innovation
se: The meeting considered ways to help people live long, healthy lives using science, technology and health innovation, and invited a pharmacist to brief the meeting. The next meeting was set for Wednesday 21 October 2026.
it: Ways to help people live long, healthy lives using science, technology and health innovation
